a.title: The answer

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: The answer: A ticket count per job is its share. Lottery draws

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: one random ticket per slice: the share arrives on average, with

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: no state but the counts. Stride keeps a pass per job, runs the

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: lowest and adds its stride: the share is exact every cycle. The

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: costs: a newcomer's pass, and nobody saying where the tickets

a.title: The answer

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: The answer: Each CPU has a cache, so a move can cost a job a

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: refill of its cache (in the measurements, a move every

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: millisecond or two made the run 1.7 to 3.3 times slower: 0.5 to

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: 1.2 ms per move, about what refetching the whole list would

text.font-family: Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif

a.text: cost): keep a job where it last ran, which is cache affinity. …
